title: "SLURM Guide"

## Submitting Jobs via Hydra

The project uses `hydra-submitit-launcher` to submit SLURM jobs directly from the command line.

### Single Run

```bash
python -m src.main -m hydra/launcher=slurm \
  method=sart dataset=math_synthetic scale=server
```

This creates an `sbatch` job with the settings from `configs/hydra/launcher/slurm.yaml`:

- 1 GPU, 4 CPUs, 64 GB memory, 24-hour timeout
- Partition: `gpu` (adjust in YAML for your cluster)

### Multi-Method Sweep

```bash
# Compare all methods on all datasets (39 jobs)
python -m src.main -m hydra/launcher=slurm \
  method=sft,data_filtering,jtt,focal_loss,group_dro,irm,vrex,fishr,lff,influence_filtering,meta_reweight,self_consistency,sart \
  dataset=math_synthetic,financial_synthetic,causal_synthetic
```

### Hyperparameter Search

```bash
# Optuna sweep via SLURM
python -m src.main -m hydra/launcher=slurm \
  mode=optuna method=sart optuna.n_trials=100
```

---

## SLURM Configuration

Edit `configs/hydra/launcher/slurm.yaml` to match your cluster:

```yaml
partition: gpu          # your SLURM partition name
gpus_per_node: 1        # GPUs per job
mem_gb: 64              # memory per job
timeout_min: 1440       # 24 hours
cpus_per_task: 4        # CPU cores
```

---

## Monitoring

```bash
# Check job status
squeue -u $USER

# View job output
cat outputs/<date>/<time>/.submitit/<job_id>/<job_id>_0_log.out

# Cancel all jobs
scancel -u $USER
```

---

## Cluster-Specific Notes

- Ensure `torch`, `hydra-core`, and `hydra-submitit-launcher` are available in the SLURM environment
- Use `module load` commands in `setup` field of `slurm.yaml` if needed
- For multi-GPU jobs, adjust `gpus_per_node` and `tasks_per_node`
